# clj-ui

> clj-ui is a cross-target Clojure UI framework: one `.cljc` component renders to Hiccup (server-side, no JS), Replicant (ClojureScript) and Squint (Eucalypt). Design tokens are EDN and the CSS is generated by Babashka; interactive behavior ships as a small JS runtime. 46 components, 20 with full agent docs.

Component links point to per-component markdown with when to use, when not to, usage, props, keyboard, accessibility, motion, responsive and per-target notes.

## Install

Add the framework as a git dependency in `bb.edn` or `deps.edn`:

```edn
{:deps {clj-ui-framework/clj-ui-framework
        {:git/url "https://github.com/floscr/clj-ui-framework" :git/sha "<sha>"}}}
```

Generate the CSS once (tokens + every component style) and load the JS runtime for interactive components:

```clojure
(require '[ui.css.gen :as css])
(def theme-css  (css/build-css))   ; CSS string, or (css/build-css {:output "public/ui.css"})
(def runtime-js (css/build-js))    ; ui-runtime.js string
```

Dark mode: `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` (auto via prefers-color-scheme otherwise). Accent: `data-accent` = neutral, blue, teal, green, amber, orange, red, pink.

## Rules for agents

- Prefer an existing clj-ui component over new markup; compose components, never restyle their internals.
- Read the component's markdown before using it and use only documented props. Follow its "When not to use".
- Components are `.cljc`: one call renders to Hiccup (`:clj`), Replicant (`:cljs`) and Squint. Mind the target table in each page (events, `:class` vector vs string, `:style` shape).
- Use the semantic tokens (`--bg-0/1/2`, `--fg-0/1/2`, `--accent`, `--accent-subtle`, `--danger`, `--success`, `--warning`, `--border-0`, `--border-subtle`, `--radius-control/panel/surface`, `--size-N`, `--font-*`) instead of raw colors or rem values, and check light and dark themes.
- Motion: `--duration-fast/standard/considered` with `--ease-standard`; animate transform, opacity and color only. Reduced motion is handled globally.
- Copy: sentence case, verbs with objects on buttons, no eyebrow labels, no uppercase transforms, weights 400 and 500 only.
- Interactive behavior that hiccup cannot express lives in the JS runtime (ui-runtime.js); load it once per page.

## Docs

- [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md): contributor guide, target pitfalls, theme system, how to add a component
- [components.md](components.md): index with public API per component
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): this file with every component page inlined

## Components

### Actions

- [Button](components/button.md): A single action with quiet secondary states, press feedback and a loading spinner.
- [Command palette](components/command.md): A searchable command menu in a native dialog with groups, icons, shortcut hints, a global hotkey and Alt quick-select.
- [Context menu](components/context-menu.md): Secondary actions close to the object: a right-click (or long-press on touch) menu for any wrapped element.

### Inputs

- [Form](components/form.md): Labeled fields, inputs, textareas, checkboxes, radios, file and range inputs, joined groups and a search bar.
- [Select](components/select.md): A compact choice field with a framework-drawn listbox, keyboard navigation and form support.
- [Switch](components/switch.md): A toggle for a setting that takes effect immediately.

### Disclosure

- [Accordion](components/accordion.md): Progressively reveal supporting content in place, using native details and summary with no JS.
- [Breadcrumb](components/breadcrumb.md): Shows where a page sits in a hierarchy; every item but the last is a link.
- [Dialog](components/dialog.md): A focused modal surface for decisions that need attention, as a native <dialog> or an overlay for reactive apps.
- [Popover](components/popover.md): A small anchored panel for contextual controls, built on the native Popover API so it works without app state.
- [Tabs](components/tabs.md): Switch between peer panels of one object, with no JS: hidden radios drive the panels.
- [Tooltip](components/tooltip.md): Short supporting text for an unfamiliar control, shown on hover and focus with pure CSS.

### Feedback

- [Alert](components/alert.md): A persistent inline message with a tone, icon and optional title that helps people recover or continue.
- [Progress](components/progress.md): Shows how much of a known task is complete as a filled track.
- [Skeleton](components/skeleton.md): Reserves space with a pulsing placeholder while content loads.
- [Toast](components/toast.md): A brief floating confirmation for completed background work, shown by the JS runtime on every target.

### Data

- [Badge](components/badge.md): A small pill for status, category or a count, with an optional leading icon.
- [Card](components/card.md): A bordered surface that groups related content and actions, plus a divided list variant.
- [Pagination](components/pagination.md): Move through a long collection with numbered pages and previous and next links.
- [Table](components/table.md): Records in columns from a headers vector and row vectors, with striped and bordered variants.

### Not yet categorized

- [button-group](components/button-group.md): Button group — a cluster of related buttons rendered as a segmented (no metadata yet)
- [calendar](components/calendar.md): Month-grid date picker. See src/ui/calendar.md for full documentation. (no metadata yet)
- [calendar-events](components/calendar-events.md): Event-aware calendar components. See src/ui/calendar.md for full documentation. (no metadata yet)
- [camera](components/camera.md): Camera capture: capability detection, getUserMedia stream helpers, and (no metadata yet)
- [chat](components/chat.md): Chat conversation components: message log, bubbles, thinking indicator, (no metadata yet)
- [chip](components/chip.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [color-picker](components/color-picker.md): Color picker — saturation/brightness plane, hue and opacity tracks, format switch and CSS value field. (no metadata yet)
- [drop-zone](components/drop-zone.md): Drag & drop file upload zone. (no metadata yet)
- [empty-state](components/empty-state.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [file-browser](components/file-browser.md): File browser components — grid/list views. (no metadata yet)
- [file-progress](components/file-progress.md): File progress list — shows files with upload/processing status. (no metadata yet)
- [grid](components/grid.md): Responsive tile grid with square and masonry layouts, plus toolbar (no metadata yet)
- [icon](components/icon.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [lightbox](components/lightbox.md): Lightbox component for fullscreen image viewing. (no metadata yet)
- [markdown](components/markdown.md): Minimal markdown-to-hiccup renderer for dev documentation pages. (no metadata yet)
- [number-field](components/number-field.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [panels](components/panels.md): Resizable panel groups — a port of motion-panels (no metadata yet)
- [player-bar](components/player-bar.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [processing-bar](components/processing-bar.md): Processing bar — compact panel showing background jobs in progress. (no metadata yet)
- [separator](components/separator.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [sidebar](components/sidebar.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [spinner](components/spinner.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [tag-input](components/tag-input.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [theme-toggle](components/theme-toggle.md):  (no metadata yet)
- [timeline](components/timeline.md): Motion-Studio-style editing timeline — ruler with ticks, labeled tracks (no metadata yet)
- [toolbar](components/toolbar.md): Toolbar — a rounded container that groups buttons (typically icon buttons) (no metadata yet)

# Accordion

> Progressively reveal supporting content in place, using native details and summary with no JS.

- Type: Component (disclosure, Navigation)
- Namespace: `ui.accordion`
- Source: `src/ui/accordion.cljc`
- Public fns: `accordion-class-list`, `accordion-classes`, `accordion`
- Keywords: accordion, collapsible, details, faq, expand

## When to use

- Stacked sections read in order where most people only need some: FAQ, advanced settings, long help.
- Content that must collapse on server-rendered pages without JS.

## When not to use

- Use tabs for peer panels of one object where one is always visible.
- Use dialog or popover for content that should float over the page.
- Do not hide the primary content of a page in a collapsed accordion.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.accordion :as accordion])

[:div
 (accordion/accordion {:title "What is this framework?" :open true}
   [:p "A cross-target component library for Clojure."])
 (accordion/accordion {:title "How do I use it?"}
   [:p "Require the namespace and call the functions."])]
```

## API reference

### `accordion`

One collapsible item: <details> with a styled <summary> and a chevron. Stack several for a group; adjacent items join their borders.

Children: The revealed content.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:title` | `string` | – | Trigger text. |
| `:open` | `boolean` | – | Initially expanded. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – | For example {:name "faq"} to make items exclusive in supporting browsers. |

### `accordion-classes`

Class string for the item.

### `accordion-class-list`

Vector form.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Toggles the focused item (native summary). |

## Accessibility

- Native details and summary expose the expanded state without ARIA.
- The chevron is aria-hidden; the title is the accessible name.

## Motion

- The chevron rotates and the trigger tints over --duration-fast. Height does not animate.

## Responsive behavior

- Full width of its column; the title wraps.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Works without JS. State is browser-side only.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Uncontrolled; listen for the toggle event via :attrs if you must react.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Uncontrolled; never pass :open false, use (when x true).

## Notes for AI

- Titles are questions or short labels in sentence case.
- For a FAQ, keep one item open by default on first paint.

## Related

- [Tabs](tabs.md): Switch between peer panels of one object, with no JS: hidden radios drive the panels.
- [Card](card.md): A bordered surface that groups related content and actions, plus a divided list variant.

## Guidance for AI tools

Accordion: Progressively reveal supporting content in place, using native details and summary with no JS. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Alert

> A persistent inline message with a tone, icon and optional title that helps people recover or continue.

- Type: Component (feedback, Messages)
- Namespace: `ui.alert`
- Source: `src/ui/alert.cljc`
- Public fns: `alert-class-list`, `alert-classes`, `alert`
- Keywords: alert, banner, error message, warning, info, inline feedback

## When to use

- An error next to its cause, with how to fix it (We could not save. Check your connection and try again).
- A warning or notice that stays until the situation changes.
- A success state that needs more than a label change, for example after a multi-step import.

## When not to use

- Use toast for brief confirmation of background work.
- Use badge for a one-word status.
- Use form-field :error for a single field's validation message.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.alert :as alert])

(alert/alert {:variant :danger :title "Could not save"}
  "Check your connection and try again.")
```

## Examples

### Neutral notice without an icon

```clojure
(alert/alert {:icon-name false} "Changes apply after the next deploy.")
```

### Custom icon

```clojure
(alert/alert {:variant :info :icon-name :zap :title "New"} "Keyboard shortcuts are available.")
```

## API reference

### `alert`

Renders a tinted panel with icon, title and body.

Children: The message body.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:variant` | `:success \| :warning \| :danger \| :info \| nil` | `nil (neutral)` | Tone; picks the tint and the default icon. |
| `:title` | `string` | – | Optional bold first line. |
| `:icon-name` | `icon keyword \| false` | – | Override the tone's icon, or false to hide it. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `alert-classes`

Class string for {:variant}.

### `alert-class-list`

Vector form.

## Accessibility

- Tone is never the only signal: the title or body names the situation.
- For messages that appear after an action, add :attrs {:role "status"} (or "alert" for errors) so screen readers announce them.

## Motion

- None; alerts should not shift layout when they appear, reserve the space or place them at the top of the region.

## Responsive behavior

- Full width of its column; the body wraps.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static markup.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: :class may be a vector.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Static markup.

## Notes for AI

- Error copy says what happened and how to fix it; no exclamation marks.
- One alert per region. Do not stack alerts for a single problem.

## Related

- [Toast](toast.md): A brief floating confirmation for completed background work, shown by the JS runtime on every target.
- [Badge](badge.md): A small pill for status, category or a count, with an optional leading icon.
- `empty-state`

## Guidance for AI tools

Alert: A persistent inline message with a tone, icon and optional title that helps people recover or continue. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Badge

> A small pill for status, category or a count, with an optional leading icon.

- Type: Component (data, Status)
- Namespace: `ui.badge`
- Source: `src/ui/badge.cljc`
- Public fns: `badge-class-list`, `badge-classes`, `badge`
- Keywords: status, tag, label, pill, count

## When to use

- Status next to a record: Active, Pending, Failed (use the matching tone).
- A category or type marker in a list or table cell.
- Emphasis beside a heading: Recommended, New, Beta (use :primary).

## When not to use

- Use chip for a selectable or removable token (filters, tag inputs).
- Use alert for a message with a sentence of text and an action.
- Do not use status tones for decoration; green means success, red means failure.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.badge :as badge])

(badge/badge {:variant :success :icon-name :check} "Verified")
```

## Examples

### Outline and compact

```clojure
(badge/badge {:variant :outline :size :sm} "Draft")
```

### Count

```clojure
(badge/badge {:variant :secondary} "12")
```

## API reference

### `badge`

Renders an inline <span> pill.

Children: The label text.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:variant` | `:primary \| :secondary \| :outline \| :success \| :warning \| :danger` | `:primary` | Tone. :primary uses the accent and is for emphasis; the status tones are for real status. |
| `:icon-name` | `icon keyword` | – | Optional leading icon at the small size. |
| `:size` | `:sm` | – | Compact variant. |
| `:class` | `string` | – | Extra classes. |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – | Extra HTML attributes. |

### `badge-classes`

Class string for {:variant :size}.

### `badge-class-list`

Vector form of badge-classes.

## Accessibility

- A badge is plain text; the tone must never be the only carrier of meaning, so the label says the status.
- Decorative icons inside a badge are aria-hidden by the icon component.

## Motion

- None.

## Responsive behavior

- Text does not wrap; keep labels to one or two words.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static markup.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: :class may be a vector.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Static markup; keywords are strings.

## Notes for AI

- Pair every status badge with the word for the status; never a colored dot alone.
- Use :primary only for emphasis (Recommended, New), not for a status.

## Related

- `chip`
- [Alert](alert.md): A persistent inline message with a tone, icon and optional title that helps people recover or continue.
- `icon`

## Guidance for AI tools

Badge: A small pill for status, category or a count, with an optional leading icon. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Breadcrumb

> Shows where a page sits in a hierarchy; every item but the last is a link.

- Type: Component (disclosure, Navigation)
- Namespace: `ui.breadcrumb`
- Source: `src/ui/breadcrumb.cljc`
- Public fns: `breadcrumb`
- Keywords: breadcrumb, hierarchy, navigation path, ancestors

## When to use

- Pages nested two or more levels deep: Projects, Harbour, Settings.
- Record pages where people jump back up a level often.

## When not to use

- Top-level sections belong in the sidebar or header, not a breadcrumb.
- Use pagination for sequential pages of one collection.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.breadcrumb :as breadcrumb])

(breadcrumb/breadcrumb {:items [{:label "Projects" :href "/projects"}
                                {:label "Harbour" :href "/projects/harbour"}
                                {:label "Settings"}]})
```

## API reference

### `breadcrumb`

Renders <nav aria-label=Breadcrumb> with an ordered list. The last item is the current page and is not a link.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:items` | `vector of {:label :href}` | – | Ancestors first; the last item needs no :href. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – | Attributes on the <ol>. |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves through the links. |

## Accessibility

- Landmark nav with a label; the current item is plain text.
- Add {:aria-current "page"} on the last item via :attrs on the list if your app relies on it.

## Motion

- None.

## Responsive behavior

- Below about 560px hide the root item or truncate long labels; the list does not wrap by default.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static links.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Static links; use your router's href scheme.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Static links.

## Notes for AI

- Labels mirror the page titles exactly.
- Three to four levels at most; collapse deeper paths.

## Related

- [Pagination](pagination.md): Move through a long collection with numbered pages and previous and next links.
- `sidebar`
- [Tabs](tabs.md): Switch between peer panels of one object, with no JS: hidden radios drive the panels.

## Guidance for AI tools

Breadcrumb: Shows where a page sits in a hierarchy; every item but the last is a link. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Button

> A single action with quiet secondary states, press feedback and a loading spinner.

- Type: Component (actions, Buttons)
- Namespace: `ui.button`
- Source: `src/ui/button.cljc`
- Public fns: `button-class-list`, `button-classes`, `button`
- Keywords: action, submit, loading button, icon button, link button, press feedback

## When to use

- Any single action on a page, form or dialog: Save, Continue, Cancel.
- Short async work where a spinner on the button is enough feedback (:loading).
- Icon-only actions in toolbars and headers (:icon), optionally :round.

## When not to use

- Use button-group for two to five related options that act as one segmented control.
- Use toolbar for a cluster of icon buttons that should read as one surface.
- Use a plain link for navigation inside body text; :href on a button is for call-to-action styling only.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.button :as button])

(button/button {:variant :primary :icon-left :plus :on-click save!}
  "Add item")
```

## Examples

### Loading state

```clojure
(button/button {:variant :primary :loading saving?} "Save changes")
```

### Icon-only, round

```clojure
(button/button {:icon :x :round true :variant :ghost
                :attrs {:aria-label "Close"}})
```

### Link styled as a button

```clojure
(button/button {:href "/docs" :variant :secondary :icon-right :arrow-right}
  "Read the docs")
```

### Hiccup with an inline handler

```clojure
(button/button {:variant :danger :attrs {:onclick "deleteItem()"}} "Delete item")
```

## API reference

### `button`

Renders a <button>, or an <a> when :href is set.

Children: The label (text, icons, any hiccup).

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:variant` | `:primary \| :secondary \| :ghost \| :danger \| :success \| :link` | `:secondary` | Visual weight. One :primary action per surface. |
| `:size` | `:sm \| :md \| :lg` | `:md` | Height, padding and icon size. |
| `:href` | `string` | – | Render as an anchor pointing at this URL. |
| `:on-click` | `fn` | – | Click handler on :cljs and :squint. Ignored on :clj (use :attrs). |
| `:disabled` | `boolean` | – | Disables the control. The attribute is emitted only when true. |
| `:loading` | `boolean` | – | Shows a spinner in place of the leading icon and disables the button. |
| `:icon-left` | `icon keyword` | – | Leading icon, e.g. :plus. |
| `:icon-right` | `icon keyword` | – | Trailing icon, e.g. :arrow-right. |
| `:icon` | `icon keyword` | – | Icon-only button (no children). Add an aria-label via :attrs. |
| `:round` | `boolean` | – | Fully round shape for icon-only buttons. |
| `:class` | `string` | – | Extra classes for layout. |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – | Extra HTML attributes merged onto the element (id, aria-*, data-*, onclick on :clj). |

### `button-classes`

Class string for {:variant :size :icon :round :loading}. Use it to style another element like a button, for example a popover-trigger or a label.

### `button-class-list`

Same as button-classes but returns a vector of class tokens (what Replicant needs).

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Activates the button. |

## Accessibility

- Native <button> (or <a> with :href), so role and focus come for free.
- Icon-only buttons need an aria-label through :attrs.
- Loading sets disabled, so focus can move away; keep loading operations short.

## Motion

- Presses scale to 0.97 (0.94 for icon buttons) over --duration-fast.
- Hover changes color only. Reduced motion drops the press scale.

## Responsive behavior

- Size is fixed by :size; pick :lg for primary touch targets.
- Hover styles apply only on hover-capable pointers (gated by the CSS build).

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: No event handlers. Use :attrs {:onclick "..."} or HTMX attributes.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: :on-click becomes {:on {:click f}}; :class may be a vector of tokens.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: :on-click is passed as a flat attribute; keywords are strings at runtime.

## Notes for AI

- The default variant is :secondary. Set :variant :primary on the one main action of a surface.
- Pass a changing label as children (Save, then Saved) instead of swapping two buttons.
- Never hand-write <button class="btn">; call the component so loading, icons and disabled stay consistent.
- Destructive actions use :variant :danger with a verb plus object label (Delete project).

## Related

- `button-group`: Button group — a cluster of related buttons rendered as a segmented
- `toolbar`: Toolbar — a rounded container that groups buttons (typically icon buttons)
- `spinner`
- `icon`

## Guidance for AI tools

Button: A single action with quiet secondary states, press feedback and a loading spinner. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Card

> A bordered surface that groups related content and actions, plus a divided list variant.

- Type: Component (data, Surfaces)
- Namespace: `ui.card`
- Source: `src/ui/card.cljc`
- Public fns: `card-class-list`, `card-classes`, `card`, `card-header`, `card-body`, `card-footer`, `card-list-class-list`, `card-list-classes`, `card-list`, `card-list-item`
- Keywords: card, panel, surface, list, settings rows, section

## When to use

- Grouping a title, body and actions that belong together (a form section, a summary).
- A list of rows on one surface with hairline dividers (card-list), for settings or options.
- A real boundary between regions of a page. Prefer proximity and spacing first, a card second.

## When not to use

- Do not nest cards inside cards; use card-list rows or plain spacing inside a card.
- Use dialog for content that must interrupt, popover for a small anchored panel.
- Use table for records with columns.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.card :as card])

(card/card {}
  (card/card-header {} [:h3 "Card title"] [:p "Description"])
  (card/card-body {} "Content")
  (card/card-footer {}
    (button/button {} "Cancel")
    (button/button {:variant :primary} "Save changes")))
```

## Examples

### Divided list with inset dividers

```clojure
(card/card-list {:divider :inset}
  (card/card-list-item {} "Notifications")
  (card/card-list-item {} "Privacy")
  (card/card-list-item {} "Appearance"))
```

### Flush card with sections

```clojure
(card/card {:class "card-flush"}
  [:div.card-section "Header row"]
  [:div.card-section "Body row"])
```

## API reference

### `card`

The surface: bg-1 background, border-0, radius-surface, no shadow. Add class card-flush to remove padding and use .card-section children with dividers.

Children: Any hiccup; usually card-header, card-body, card-footer.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – | Extra classes (card-flush for a padding-less card). |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – | Extra HTML attributes. |

### `card-header`

Title block; headings inside lose their margin, a <p> renders as the muted description.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `card-body`

Main content; first and last child margins are trimmed.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `card-footer`

Right-aligned action row.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `card-list`

A card surface whose children are rows separated by hairline dividers.

Children: card-list-item elements.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:divider` | `:full \| :inset` | `:full` | Edge-to-edge dividers or dividers inset from the sides. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `card-list-item`

One row of a card-list.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `card-classes`

Class string for a card.

### `card-list-classes`

Class string for {:divider}.

## Accessibility

- A card is a <div>; add a heading inside card-header so the region has a name.
- Interactive rows in a card-list should be real buttons or links, not clickable divs.

## Motion

- None.

## Responsive behavior

- Cards fill their column; the page sets gutters. Side-by-side cards share the same top and height (align-items stretch).
- Wide tables inside a card scroll inside the card, not the page.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static markup.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: :class may be a vector.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Static markup.

## Notes for AI

- Nested radii are concentric: inner = outer minus padding. Use calc(var(--radius-surface) - var(--size-6)) for media inside a padded card.
- Settings pages are one card-list per section with label-plus-control rows, not one card per row.

## Related

- [Dialog](dialog.md): A focused modal surface for decisions that need attention, as a native <dialog> or an overlay for reactive apps.
- [Popover](popover.md): A small anchored panel for contextual controls, built on the native Popover API so it works without app state.
- [Table](table.md): Records in columns from a headers vector and row vectors, with striped and bordered variants.
- [Accordion](accordion.md): Progressively reveal supporting content in place, using native details and summary with no JS.

## Guidance for AI tools

Card: A bordered surface that groups related content and actions, plus a divided list variant. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Command palette

> A searchable command menu in a native dialog with groups, icons, shortcut hints, a global hotkey and Alt quick-select.

- Type: Component (actions, Menus)
- Namespace: `ui.command`
- Source: `src/ui/command.cljc`
- Public fns: `command-item`, `command-group`, `command-dialog`, `command-trigger`
- JS runtime: `ui.js.command` (bundled in ui-runtime.js)
- Keywords: command palette, cmdk, search commands, keyboard, hotkey, quick switcher

## When to use

- Global search and actions behind one hotkey (mod+k): navigate, create, switch.
- A long list that needs filtering and keyboard selection, such as a file or page switcher.

## When not to use

- Use select for one of many values in a form.
- Use context-menu for actions on a specific object under the pointer.
- Use form search-bar for a search that submits and shows results on a page.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.command :as command])

(command/command-trigger {:target "cmdk" :class (button/button-classes {})} "Search…")

(command/command-dialog {:id "cmdk" :placeholder "Type a command or search…" :hotkey "mod+k"}
  (command/command-group {:heading "Pages"}
    (command/command-item {:icon :calendar :url "/calendar" :shortcut "⌘P"} "Calendar")
    (command/command-item {:icon :settings :url "/settings"} "Settings")))
```

## Examples

### Recents and search-only rows

```clojure
(command/command-group {:heading "Recent"}
  (command/command-item {:value "" :url "/p/42"} "Harbour redesign"))
(command/command-group {:heading "Archive"}
  (command/command-item {:search-only true :url "/p/7" :description "Archived 2025"} "Old site"))
```

### Alt quick-select with letters

```clojure
(command/command-dialog {:id "cmdk" :hotkey "mod+k" :quick-nav :letters} ...)
```

## API reference

### `command-dialog`

The palette: a native <dialog> with a search input and the item list. The runtime filters, navigates and selects.

Children: command-group and command-item forms.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:id` | `string` | – | Matched by command-trigger :target (required). |
| `:placeholder` | `string` | `"Type a command or search…"` |  |
| `:hotkey` | `string` | – | Global open shortcut, e.g. "mod+k" (mod is ⌘ on Mac, Ctrl elsewhere). |
| `:quick-nav` | `:letters \| :numbers \| string` | – | Hold Alt to show key badges on the visible rows; Alt+key selects. Off by default. |
| `:empty` | `string` | `"No results found."` | Empty-state text. |
| `:leading` | `hiccup` | – | Replaces the search icon, e.g. a back button. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `command-group`

Groups items under an optional heading. While searching, groups flatten into one ranked list.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:heading` | `string` | – |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `command-item`

One row: a <button>, or an <a> when :url is set. Selection closes the dialog.

Children: The label.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:icon` | `icon keyword` | – |  |
| `:shortcut` | `string` | – | Shortcut hint shown as a kbd, e.g. "⌘P". |
| `:description` | `string` | – | Secondary line under the label. |
| `:url` | `string` | – | Navigate on select. |
| `:value` | `string` | – | Explicit search text. An empty string shows the row only while the input is empty (recents). |
| `:search-only` | `boolean` | – | Hide while the input is empty; surface only as a search result. |
| `:on-click` | `fn` | – | Selection callback (:cljs and :squint). |
| `:disabled` | `boolean` | – |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `command-trigger`

A <button> that opens the matching dialog.

Children: The trigger label.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:target` | `string` | – | Id of the command-dialog (required). |
| `:class` | `string` | – | Usually a button class string. |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| mod+k (or :hotkey) | Opens the palette. |
| Type | Filters items live; groups flatten into one ranked list. |
| ArrowUp / ArrowDown, Ctrl+j / Ctrl+k | Move the highlighted row. |
| Enter | Selects the highlighted row. |
| Alt+key | Selects the badged row when :quick-nav is on. |
| Escape | Closes. |

## Accessibility

- The dialog is a native <dialog> (focus trap, Escape); items have role=option inside role=group.
- The trigger carries aria-haspopup=dialog.

## Motion

- The dialog fades and scales in over --duration-fast with --ease-enter.

## Responsive behavior

- The dialog is capped to the viewport; on phones it fills the width and the list scrolls.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static markup plus ui-runtime.js; items navigate via :url.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Items may use :on-click; the dialog stays uncontrolled.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Same as Replicant. The runtime re-filters when rows are patched in place.

## Notes for AI

- One palette per app, opened from a trigger in the header and the hotkey.
- Give every item a verb or a destination as its label; use :description for context, not for a second label.

## Related

- [Select](select.md): A compact choice field with a framework-drawn listbox, keyboard navigation and form support.
- [Context menu](context-menu.md): Secondary actions close to the object: a right-click (or long-press on touch) menu for any wrapped element.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): A focused modal surface for decisions that need attention, as a native <dialog> or an overlay for reactive apps.
- [Form](form.md): Labeled fields, inputs, textareas, checkboxes, radios, file and range inputs, joined groups and a search bar.

## Guidance for AI tools

Command palette: A searchable command menu in a native dialog with groups, icons, shortcut hints, a global hotkey and Alt quick-select. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Context menu

> Secondary actions close to the object: a right-click (or long-press on touch) menu for any wrapped element.

- Type: Component (actions, Menus)
- Namespace: `ui.context-menu`
- Source: `src/ui/context_menu.cljc`
- Public fns: `icon-paths-for`, `normalize-item`, `context-menu-trigger`
- JS runtime: `ui.js.context-menu`, `ui.js.gestures` (bundled in ui-runtime.js)
- Keywords: context menu, right click, long press, actions menu, row actions

## When to use

- Secondary actions on a specific object: a file, a row, a tile, a message.
- Actions that should stay out of the way until asked for, on desktop and touch alike.

## When not to use

- Use command for global actions and search.
- Use popover for a panel with controls, not a list of actions.
- Put primary actions in visible buttons; a menu must never be the only way to reach an important action.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.context-menu :as context-menu])

(context-menu/context-menu-trigger
  {:items [{:label "Edit" :url "/edit/123" :icon :edit}
           {:type :separator}
           {:label "Delete" :url "/del/123" :icon :trash :variant :danger :confirm true}]}
  [:div.file-tile "report.pdf"])
```

## Examples

### Callbacks in Replicant or Squint

```clojure
(context-menu/context-menu-trigger
  {:items [{:label "Rename" :icon :edit :on-click #(rename! id)}
           {:label "Delete" :icon :trash :variant :danger
            :confirm "Delete this file permanently?" :on-click #(delete! id)}]}
  tile)
```

## API reference

### `context-menu-trigger`

Wraps children in a trigger element. The menu itself is built by the JS runtime on contextmenu.

Children: The element that owns the actions.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:items` | `vector of item maps` | – | {:label :url :icon :variant :confirm :on-click} or {:type :separator}. :variant :danger tints the row; :confirm true (or a string) asks before running. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `normalize-item`

Flattens an item map for the runtime (adds :icon-paths, stringifies keywords).

### `icon-paths-for`

SVG child elements for an icon name, for the runtime to draw without the icon module.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Shift+F10 / Menu key | Opens the menu on the focused trigger (native contextmenu). |
| ArrowUp / ArrowDown | Move between items. |
| Enter | Runs the item. |
| Escape | Closes. |

## Accessibility

- Items are real buttons or links inside the runtime menu; disabled items use aria-disabled.
- Long-press on touch is handled globally by the gestures runtime; the pressed element shows press feedback.

## Motion

- The menu scales in from its corner over --duration-fast with --ease-enter and is clamped to the viewport.

## Responsive behavior

- On touch, a 500ms long-press opens the menu; the iOS callout is suppressed on the trigger.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Items are serialized into a data attribute; :url drives navigation.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Items are passed to the runtime directly; :on-click works.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Same as Replicant.

## Notes for AI

- Add :data-long-press to any element with a custom contextmenu handler so touch users get the same menu.
- Destructive items: :variant :danger plus :confirm; label with verb and object.

## Related

- [Command palette](command.md): A searchable command menu in a native dialog with groups, icons, shortcut hints, a global hotkey and Alt quick-select.
- [Popover](popover.md): A small anchored panel for contextual controls, built on the native Popover API so it works without app state.
- [Button](button.md): A single action with quiet secondary states, press feedback and a loading spinner.

## Guidance for AI tools

Context menu: Secondary actions close to the object: a right-click (or long-press on touch) menu for any wrapped element. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Dialog

> A focused modal surface for decisions that need attention, as a native <dialog> or an overlay for reactive apps.

- Type: Component (disclosure, Overlays)
- Namespace: `ui.dialog`
- Source: `src/ui/dialog.cljc`
- Public fns: `dialog-class-list`, `dialog-classes`, `dialog`, `dialog-overlay`, `dialog-panel`, `dialog-header`, `dialog-body`, `dialog-footer`
- Keywords: modal, dialog, confirm, overlay, showModal

## When to use

- A decision that must interrupt: confirm a destructive action, pick before continuing.
- A short form (one to four fields) that returns to the page afterwards.

## When not to use

- Use popover for small anchored controls that should not dim the page.
- Use card or a route for long forms and record detail.
- Do not open a dialog for every delete; a danger button with a clear label is enough for reversible actions.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.dialog :as dialog])

;; Native <dialog>, opened with showModal()
(dialog/dialog {:id "confirm"}
  (dialog/dialog-header {} [:h3 "Delete project?"])
  (dialog/dialog-body {} "Its 12 files are removed for everyone.")
  (dialog/dialog-footer {}
    (button/button {:attrs {:onclick "confirm.close()"}} "Cancel")
    (button/button {:variant :danger} "Delete project")))
```

## Examples

### Overlay dialog driven by app state (Squint, Replicant)

```clojure
(when open?
  (dialog/dialog-overlay {:on-close #(close!)}
    (dialog/dialog-panel {}
      (dialog/dialog-header {} [:h3 "Rename"])
      (dialog/dialog-body {} (form/form-input {:value name :on-change set-name!}))
      (dialog/dialog-footer {}
        (button/button {:on-click close!} "Cancel")
        (button/button {:variant :primary :on-click save!} "Save changes")))))
```

## API reference

### `dialog`

Native <dialog>. Open it with element.showModal() for a backdrop and focus trapping; clicking the backdrop closes it.

Children: dialog-header, dialog-body, dialog-footer.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:open` | `boolean` | – | Render open (non-modal) on first paint. |
| `:id` | `string` | – | Id used to call showModal() / close(). |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `dialog-overlay`

Backdrop that covers the viewport and centers its children. For frameworks where a native <dialog> is impractical.

Children: A dialog-panel.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:on-close` | `fn` | – | Called when the backdrop is clicked. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `dialog-panel`

The surface inside an overlay: bg-1, radius-surface, floating shadow.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `dialog-header`

Title block.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `dialog-body`

Content block.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `dialog-footer`

Right-aligned actions.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `dialog-classes`

Class string for the dialog element.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Escape | Closes a native dialog (built in). Overlay dialogs close on backdrop click; wire Escape in the app. |
| Tab | Native dialogs trap focus inside the modal. |

## Accessibility

- Prefer the native <dialog>: role, focus trap and Escape come for free.
- Give the dialog a heading in dialog-header and reference it with aria-labelledby via :attrs.
- Overlay dialogs must return focus to the trigger when closed.

## Motion

- The panel fades and scales in over --duration-fast with --ease-enter; reduced motion keeps the fade only.

## Responsive behavior

- The panel is capped to the viewport with a margin; below 480px it fills the width.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Use the native dialog with an inline onclick calling showModal().
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Either variant; the overlay is driven by state and :on-close.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Use dialog-overlay plus dialog-panel; Eucalypt re-renders on state change.

## Notes for AI

- Name the object and the consequence in the title and body: Delete Harbour? Its 12 files are removed for everyone.
- Exactly one primary action in the footer; Cancel is secondary.

## Related

- [Popover](popover.md): A small anchored panel for contextual controls, built on the native Popover API so it works without app state.
- [Command palette](command.md): A searchable command menu in a native dialog with groups, icons, shortcut hints, a global hotkey and Alt quick-select.
- [Toast](toast.md): A brief floating confirmation for completed background work, shown by the JS runtime on every target.
- [Card](card.md): A bordered surface that groups related content and actions, plus a divided list variant.

## Guidance for AI tools

Dialog: A focused modal surface for decisions that need attention, as a native <dialog> or an overlay for reactive apps. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Form

> Labeled fields, inputs, textareas, checkboxes, radios, file and range inputs, joined groups and a search bar.

- Type: Component (inputs, Text fields)
- Namespace: `ui.form`
- Source: `src/ui/form.cljc`
- Public fns: `form-field-class-list`, `form-field-classes`, `form-field`, `form-input-class-list`, `form-input-classes`, `form-input`, `form-textarea-class-list`, `form-textarea-classes`, `form-textarea`, `form-textarea-auto`, `form-select`, `form-checkbox`, `form-radio-group`, `form-file`, `form-range`, `form-group`, `form-group-addon`, `search-bar`
- Keywords: input, textarea, form field, label, checkbox, radio, file input, range, search bar, validation

## When to use

- Any text, number, date or file entry; wrap each control in form-field for its label, hint and error.
- Inline validation: pass :error on both form-field and the input.
- A search entry with a joined button (search-bar) at the top of a list.

## When not to use

- Use switch for an on or off setting that applies immediately.
- Use select (or form-select) for one of many; use form-radio-group for two to five visible options.
- Use number-field for bounded numbers with steppers, tag-input for several values, color-picker for colors.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.form :as form])

(form/form-field {:label "Email" :hint "Used for sign-in and notifications." :error email-error}
  (form/form-input {:type :email :value email :error (some? email-error) :on-change set-email!}))
```

## Examples

### Search bar that submits as GET

```clojure
(form/search-bar {:action "/search" :placeholder "Search movies…" :button-label "Search"})
```

### Radio group

```clojure
(form/form-radio-group {:label "Preference" :radio-name "pref" :radio-value "a"
                        :options [{:value "a" :label "Option A"} {:value "b" :label "Option B"}]})
```

### Joined input and addon

```clojure
(form/form-group {}
  (form/form-group-addon {} "https://")
  (form/form-input {:placeholder "example.com"}))
```

## API reference

### `form-field`

Wrapper with label above, hint or error below. The error text also sets the error state.

Children: The control.

| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `form-input`

Single-line input. With :icon-left or :icon-right it is wrapped in .form-input-wrap.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:type` | `keyword` | `:text` | :text, :email, :password, :date, :datetime-local, ... |
| `:placeholder` | `string` | – |  |
| `:value` | `string` | – |  |
| `:disabled` | `boolean` | – |  |
| `:error` | `boolean` | – | Error styling. |

| `:on-change` | `fn` | – | :cljs and :squint only. |

### `search-bar`

Preset: icon input joined to a primary button; wrapped in a GET <form> when :action or :on-submit is set.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:name` | `string` | `"q"` |  |
| `:value` | `string` | – |  |
| `:placeholder` | `string` | `"Search…"` |  |
| `:icon` | `icon keyword` | `:search` |  |
| `:button-label` | `string` | `"Search"` |  |
| `:disabled` | `boolean` | – |  |
| `:action` | `string` | – | Form action URL. |
| `:on-change` | `fn` | – |  |
| `:on-submit` | `fn` | – |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |
| `:form-attrs` | `map` | – | Attributes on the wrapping <form>. |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves between fields. |
| Space | Toggles a checkbox or radio. |
| Arrow keys | Move within a radio group or a range. |

## Accessibility

- form-field renders a real <label>; pass an id via :attrs on the control and the label picks it up through nesting.
- Errors sit next to the field and say how to fix it; do not rely on the red border alone.
- Inputs are 44px tall by default, the phone tap minimum.

## Motion

- Border and background transitions over --duration-fast. Focus shows the shared ring.

## Responsive behavior

- Fields fill their column; forms read best at 640 to 720px wide. form-group stays on one line and scrolls its content.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Uncontrolled inputs that submit with a <form>; use :attrs for name and required.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Controlled via :value and :on-change (receives the DOM event).
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Controlled; never pass false to :disabled or :required (use (when x true)).

## Notes for AI

- One form-field per control; the label is the only heading a field needs.
- Use search-bar for the search pattern instead of assembling form-group by hand; the joined corners are easy to get wrong.
- Submit buttons are verb plus object: Save changes, Create project.

## Related

- [Select](select.md): A compact choice field with a framework-drawn listbox, keyboard navigation and form support.
- [Switch](switch.md): A toggle for a setting that takes effect immediately.
- `number-field`
- `tag-input`
- [Button](button.md): A single action with quiet secondary states, press feedback and a loading spinner.

## Guidance for AI tools

Form: Labeled fields, inputs, textareas, checkboxes, radios, file and range inputs, joined groups and a search bar. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Pagination

> Move through a long collection with numbered pages and previous and next links.

- Type: Component (data, Collections)
- Namespace: `ui.pagination`
- Source: `src/ui/pagination.cljc`
- Public fns: `pagination-item-class-list`, `pagination-item-classes`, `pagination`
- Keywords: pagination, pages, next previous, paging

## When to use

- Collections split into pages on the server, where each page has a URL.
- Tables and lists with a known total page count.

## When not to use

- Use infinite scroll or a Load more button for feeds without a meaningful page number.
- Use tabs or button-group to switch between views, not pages.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.pagination :as pagination])

(pagination/pagination {:current 3 :total 10
                        :href-fn #(str "/items?page=" %)})
```

## Examples

### Client-side paging

```clojure
(pagination/pagination {:current page :total 10 :on-click set-page!})
```

## API reference

### `pagination`

Renders <nav aria-label=Pagination> with Previous, every page number and Next.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:current` | `int` | – | Current page, 1-based. |
| `:total` | `int` | – | Total number of pages. |
| `:href-fn` | `fn [page] -> url` | – | Builds each page link (hiccup). |
| `:on-click` | `fn [page]` | – | Click handler on :cljs and :squint; prevents the default navigation. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `pagination-item-classes`

Class string for {:active :disabled}.

### `pagination-item-class-list`

Vector form.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves through the page links. |
| Enter | Follows the link. |

## Accessibility

- Links inside a labeled nav; the active page is marked by its class and should also carry aria-current via :attrs when needed.
- Disabled Previous and Next keep their href but are styled inert.

## Motion

- Hover tint over --duration-fast.

## Responsive behavior

- Every page number renders; for more than about ten pages show a window of pages in the app before passing :total.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Use :href-fn; each page is a real link.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Use :on-click for client-side paging; :href-fn is optional.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Same as Replicant.

## Notes for AI

- Numbers use tabular-nums; keep Previous and Next as words, not arrows alone.

## Related

- [Table](table.md): Records in columns from a headers vector and row vectors, with striped and bordered variants.
- [Breadcrumb](breadcrumb.md): Shows where a page sits in a hierarchy; every item but the last is a link.
- `button-group`: Button group — a cluster of related buttons rendered as a segmented

## Guidance for AI tools

Pagination: Move through a long collection with numbered pages and previous and next links. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Popover

> A small anchored panel for contextual controls, built on the native Popover API so it works without app state.

- Type: Component (disclosure, Overlays)
- Namespace: `ui.popover`
- Source: `src/ui/popover.cljc`
- Public fns: `trigger-attrs`, `content-class-list`, `popover-trigger`, `popover-content`, `popover-header`, `popover-title`, `popover-description`
- JS runtime: `ui.js.popover` (bundled in ui-runtime.js)
- Keywords: popover, anchored panel, popovertarget, dropdown panel, settings panel

## When to use

- Small anchored controls (a couple of fields, a picker) that should not dim the page.
- Contextual information next to its trigger.

## When not to use

- Use dialog for a decision that must interrupt.
- Use context-menu for a list of actions on right-click or long press.
- Use tooltip for one line of hint text.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.popover :as popover])

(popover/popover-trigger {:target "dimensions"
                          :class (button/button-classes {:variant :secondary})}
  "Open")
(popover/popover-content {:id "dimensions" :side :bottom :align :start}
  (popover/popover-header {}
    (popover/popover-title {} "Dimensions")
    (popover/popover-description {} "Set the dimensions for the layer."))
  (form/form-field {:label "Width"} (form/form-input {:value "100%"})))
```

## Examples

### Turn an existing button into a trigger

```clojure
(button/button {:variant :ghost :icon :settings
                :attrs (merge {:aria-label "Settings"} (popover/trigger-attrs "settings"))})
```

## API reference

### `popover-trigger`

A <button> with popovertarget pointing at the content's id.

Children: The trigger label.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:target` | `string` | – | Id of the matching popover-content (required). |
| `:class` | `string` | – | Usually a button class string. |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `popover-content`

The floating panel (popover="auto"). The JS runtime anchors it to the trigger.

Children: popover-header and any content.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:id` | `string` | – | Must match the trigger's :target (required). |
| `:side` | `:top \| :right \| :bottom \| :left` | `:bottom` | Which side of the trigger the panel opens on. |
| `:align` | `:start \| :center \| :end` | `:center` | Alignment along that side. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `popover-header`

Title block.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `popover-title`

Heading text.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `popover-description`

Muted description.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `trigger-attrs`

Attribute map {:popovertarget id :aria-haspopup "dialog"} to spread onto any element.

### `content-class-list`

Class vector for {:side}.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Escape | Closes the popover (native). |
| Enter / Space | On the trigger, toggles it. |

## Accessibility

- The trigger carries aria-haspopup=dialog; the native Popover API manages light dismiss and Escape.
- Give the panel a title so it has an accessible name.

## Motion

- The panel fades and nudges in from its side over --duration-fast; reduced motion fades only.

## Responsive behavior

- Max width is 20rem or the viewport minus a margin; the runtime flips sides when there is no room.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Works in server-rendered pages: load ui-runtime.js once.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Same markup; no state needed. Replicant keeps the popover attribute.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Same markup; ids must be stable across re-renders.

## Notes for AI

- The trigger :target and the content :id must match and be unique on the page.
- Keep the content to a few controls; a long form belongs in a dialog or a page.

## Related

- [Dialog](dialog.md): A focused modal surface for decisions that need attention, as a native <dialog> or an overlay for reactive apps.
- [Context menu](context-menu.md): Secondary actions close to the object: a right-click (or long-press on touch) menu for any wrapped element.
- [Tooltip](tooltip.md): Short supporting text for an unfamiliar control, shown on hover and focus with pure CSS.
- [Select](select.md): A compact choice field with a framework-drawn listbox, keyboard navigation and form support.

## Guidance for AI tools

Popover: A small anchored panel for contextual controls, built on the native Popover API so it works without app state. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Progress

> Shows how much of a known task is complete as a filled track.

- Type: Component (feedback, Status)
- Namespace: `ui.progress`
- Source: `src/ui/progress.cljc`
- Public fns: `progress-bar-class-list`, `progress-bar-classes`, `progress`
- Keywords: progress bar, percentage, upload progress, determinate

## When to use

- Known progress: an upload, an import, steps completed out of a total.
- Usage against a limit when paired with a label.

## When not to use

- Use spinner for unknown duration.
- Use skeleton while content is loading in place.
- Use file-progress for a list of files each with their own status.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.progress :as progress])

(progress/progress {:value 62 :attrs {:aria-label "Upload progress"}})
```

## Examples

### Tones

```clojure
(progress/progress {:value 90 :variant :warning})
(progress/progress {:value 100 :variant :success})
```

## API reference

### `progress`

A track with a fill at :value percent; role=progressbar with aria-valuenow.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:value` | `number 0 to 100` | `0` |  |
| `:variant` | `nil \| :success \| :warning \| :danger` | – | Fill tone; default is the accent. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – | Add aria-label or aria-labelledby. |

### `progress-bar-classes`

Class string for the fill given {:variant}.

### `progress-bar-class-list`

Vector form.

## Accessibility

- Exposes value, min and max; give it a name with aria-label.
- Show the percentage or count as text next to it when the number matters.

## Motion

- The fill width animates over --duration-standard.

## Responsive behavior

- Fills its column.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static; re-render to update.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Pass the live :value.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Pass the live :value; style uses string keys internally.

## Notes for AI

- Status tones only for real status: warning near a limit, danger when failed.

## Related

- `spinner`
- [Skeleton](skeleton.md): Reserves space with a pulsing placeholder while content loads.
- `file-progress`: File progress list — shows files with upload/processing status.
- `processing-bar`: Processing bar — compact panel showing background jobs in progress.

## Guidance for AI tools

Progress: Shows how much of a known task is complete as a filled track. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Select

> A compact choice field with a framework-drawn listbox, keyboard navigation and form support.

- Type: Component (inputs, Selection)
- Namespace: `ui.select`
- Source: `src/ui/select.cljc`
- Public fns: `normalize-options`, `selected-label`, `select`
- JS runtime: `ui.js.select` (bundled in ui-runtime.js)
- Keywords: select, dropdown, listbox, combobox, choice field

## When to use

- One of many options (more than about five) in a form or a toolbar.
- A choice that must look the same in every browser and both themes.

## When not to use

- Use form-radio-group for two to five visible options.
- Use command for a searchable list of actions or a long list that needs filtering.
- Use button-group to switch between views.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.select :as select])

(select/select {:options [{:value "eu" :label "Europe"}
                          {:value "us" :label "United States"}]
                :value region
                :placeholder "Pick a region"
                :on-change set-region!})
```

## Examples

### Hiccup form field (uncontrolled, submits with the form)

```clojure
(select/select {:name "region" :options ["Europe" "United States"] :value "Europe"})
```

## API reference

### `select`

Renders the trigger button; the listbox is created by the __uiSelect runtime on open.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:options` | `vector of {:value :label} or strings` | – | The choices. Bare strings use the string as value and label. |
| `:value` | `string` | – | Selected value. |
| `:placeholder` | `string` | – | Shown when nothing is selected. |
| `:disabled` | `boolean` | – |  |
| `:on-change` | `fn [value]` | – | Receives the picked value (:cljs and :squint). |
| `:name` | `string` | – | On :clj emits a hidden <input> so the value submits with a form. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `normalize-options`

Coerces strings into {:value :label} maps.

### `selected-label`

Label for the selected value, else the placeholder.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space / ArrowDown | Opens the listbox. |
| ArrowUp / ArrowDown | Moves the highlighted option. |
| Enter | Picks the highlighted option. |
| Escape | Closes without changing. |

## Accessibility

- The trigger has role=combobox with aria-haspopup=listbox and aria-expanded.
- Options are focusable rows; the selected one is marked.

## Motion

- The listbox fades and scales in over --duration-fast.

## Responsive behavior

- The listbox is capped to the viewport and scrolls; on touch the outside tap that dismisses it is consumed.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Uncontrolled; pass :name for form submission. Needs ui-runtime.js.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Controlled through :value and :on-change.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Controlled; the trigger re-renders with the new label.

## Notes for AI

- form-select in ui.form delegates here; use it inside form-field for a label and hint.
- Keep option labels short; put the long explanation in a hint.

## Related

- [Form](form.md): Labeled fields, inputs, textareas, checkboxes, radios, file and range inputs, joined groups and a search bar.
- [Command palette](command.md): A searchable command menu in a native dialog with groups, icons, shortcut hints, a global hotkey and Alt quick-select.
- [Popover](popover.md): A small anchored panel for contextual controls, built on the native Popover API so it works without app state.
- `tag-input`

## Guidance for AI tools

Select: A compact choice field with a framework-drawn listbox, keyboard navigation and form support. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Skeleton

> Reserves space with a pulsing placeholder while content loads.

- Type: Component (feedback, Status)
- Namespace: `ui.skeleton`
- Source: `src/ui/skeleton.cljc`
- Public fns: `skeleton-class-list`, `skeleton-classes`, `skeleton`
- Keywords: skeleton, loading placeholder, shimmer, lazy loading

## When to use

- Loading a region whose final layout is known: a card, a list, an avatar and name.
- First paint of data-driven views so nothing jumps when the data arrives.

## When not to use

- Use spinner for a short action with no layout to reserve, such as a button.
- Use progress when the completion is known.
- Use empty-state when loading finished and there is nothing to show.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.skeleton :as skeleton])

[:div.vstack
 (skeleton/skeleton {:variant :heading})
 (skeleton/skeleton {:variant :line})
 (skeleton/skeleton {:variant :line :class "w-full"})]
```

## Examples

### Avatar row

```clojure
[:div.hstack
 (skeleton/skeleton {:variant :circle})
 (skeleton/skeleton {:variant :line})]
```

## API reference

### `skeleton`

A pulsing block with role=status and an accessible Loading label.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:variant` | `:line \| :box \| :circle \| :heading` | – | Shape and default size. |
| `:class` | `string` | – | Size it with utilities (w-full) or a custom class. |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `skeleton-classes`

Class string for {:variant}.

### `skeleton-class-list`

Vector form.

## Accessibility

- Announces Loading once; mark the surrounding region aria-busy while skeletons show.

## Motion

- A slow pulse loops while visible; reduced motion stops it.

## Responsive behavior

- Skeletons take the dimensions of the content they stand in for; match the final layout.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static markup.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: :class may be a vector.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Static markup.

## Notes for AI

- Build the skeleton in the final layout with the same dimensions, not a generic block.

## Related

- `spinner`
- [Progress](progress.md): Shows how much of a known task is complete as a filled track.
- `empty-state`

## Guidance for AI tools

Skeleton: Reserves space with a pulsing placeholder while content loads. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Switch

> A toggle for a setting that takes effect immediately.

- Type: Component (inputs, Selection)
- Namespace: `ui.switch`
- Source: `src/ui/switch.cljc`
- Public fns: `switch-class-list`, `switch-classes`, `switch-toggle`
- Keywords: toggle, switch, on off, setting, checkbox alternative

## When to use

- A binary setting that applies as soon as it changes (notifications on, dark mode).
- Rows in a settings list where the control sits at the end of the row.

## When not to use

- Use form-checkbox inside a form that is submitted later, or for agree and include choices.
- Use button-group or tabs to switch between views of the same content.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.switch :as switch])

(switch/switch-toggle {:checked notifications?
                       :label "Email notifications"
                       :on-change #(toggle! :notifications)})
```

## Examples

### Disabled

```clojure
(switch/switch-toggle {:checked true :disabled true :label "Managed by your admin"})
```

## API reference

### `switch-toggle`

A <label> wrapping a hidden checkbox, a track and a thumb, plus the label text.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:checked` | `boolean` | – | On or off. |
| `:disabled` | `boolean` | – | Disables the input; the attribute is emitted only when true. |
| `:on-change` | `fn` | – | Change handler on :cljs and :squint. |
| `:label` | `string` | – | Visible label next to the track. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `switch-classes`

Class string for {:disabled}.

### `switch-class-list`

Vector form.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Space | Toggles the switch. |
| Tab | Moves focus to the hidden checkbox; the ring shows on the control. |

## Accessibility

- Built on a real checkbox input, so state is exposed natively.
- Always pass :label; a switch without a visible label needs an aria-label via :attrs.

## Motion

- Track color and thumb position animate over --duration-standard; reduced motion snaps.

## Responsive behavior

- The track is a fixed 40 by 22px target inside a taller label hit area.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Uncontrolled: the browser tracks the state. Submit it with a form or wire :attrs {:onchange "..."}.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Controlled: pass :checked from state and update it in :on-change.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Controlled; :disabled is omitted when falsy so Eucalypt does not disable the input.

## Notes for AI

- A switch applies immediately; if the page has a Save button, use form-checkbox instead.
- Put the label on the left and the switch on the right in settings rows.

## Related

- [Form](form.md): Labeled fields, inputs, textareas, checkboxes, radios, file and range inputs, joined groups and a search bar.
- `button-group`: Button group — a cluster of related buttons rendered as a segmented
- [Tabs](tabs.md): Switch between peer panels of one object, with no JS: hidden radios drive the panels.

## Guidance for AI tools

Switch: A toggle for a setting that takes effect immediately. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Table

> Records in columns from a headers vector and row vectors, with striped and bordered variants.

- Type: Component (data, Collections)
- Namespace: `ui.table`
- Source: `src/ui/table.cljc`
- Public fns: `table-class-list`, `table-classes`, `table`
- Keywords: table, data table, rows, columns, records

## When to use

- Structured records with the same fields per row that people compare across columns.
- Admin and settings lists with a handful of columns.

## When not to use

- Use card-list for one-column lists of options or settings rows.
- Use file-browser for files and folders with grid and list views.
- For sortable or filterable data, add controls above the table; sorting is not built in yet.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.table :as table])

(table/table {:variant :striped
              :headers ["Name" "Email" "Role"]
              :rows [["Alice Johnson" "alice@example.com" (badge/badge {:variant :success} "Active")]
                     ["Bob Smith" "bob@example.com" "Editor"]]})
```

## Examples

### Bordered, inside a card

```clojure
(card/card {:class "card-flush"}
  (table/table {:variant :bordered :headers ["Key" "Value"] :rows rows}))
```

## API reference

### `table`

Renders <table> inside a .table-wrapper that scrolls horizontally when the columns overflow.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:headers` | `vector` | – | Column header cells (strings or hiccup). |
| `:rows` | `vector of vectors` | – | Each row is a vector of cell values (strings or hiccup). |
| `:variant` | `nil \| :striped \| :bordered` | – | Zebra rows, or a bordered rounded frame. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `table-classes`

Class string for {:variant}.

### `table-class-list`

Vector form.

## Accessibility

- Real <table>, <thead> and <th> markup, so screen readers get column headers.
- Put status in a badge with a word, never color alone.

## Motion

- Row hover tint over --duration-fast.

## Responsive behavior

- Wide tables scroll inside the wrapper, not the page. On phones consider a card-list per record instead.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static markup.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: :class may be a vector.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Static markup.

## Notes for AI

- Numbers that align in a column get class tabular-nums and right alignment.
- Headers are sentence case.

## Related

- [Card](card.md): A bordered surface that groups related content and actions, plus a divided list variant.
- `file-browser`: File browser components — grid/list views.
- [Pagination](pagination.md): Move through a long collection with numbered pages and previous and next links.
- [Badge](badge.md): A small pill for status, category or a count, with an optional leading icon.

## Guidance for AI tools

Table: Records in columns from a headers vector and row vectors, with striped and bordered variants. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt
